dedupe_keys.name: galileo emergency warning satellite service pilot demonstrations 2023 to 2025

description: This testbed and emergency-response case covers the trials of the Galileo Emergency Warning Satellite Service (EWSS), which uses the messaging capacity of the Galileo navigation signal to send public warnings straight to smartphones and other Galileo receivers in a danger area, without needing mobile networks. Alerts follow a Common Alert Message Format that carries the issuing authority, hazard type, severity, timing, affected area and safety instructions in national languages, and the service is meant to reach everyone in the area within 60 seconds on average, including where networks are congested, damaged or absent. The STELLAR consortium and EUSPA ran demonstrations with civil protection agencies in France, Germany and Cyprus and then on the Belgium and Luxembourg border, with further field tests in Romania and Estonia; they report that alerts were sent and received in under a minute and that large populations could be warned even if terrestrial communications failed. A 2024 to 2025 pilot phase let Member State authorities try the service, and a 2025 exercise simulating a severe thunderstorm and a hazardous materials incident showed street display panels picking up the satellite alert. Coverage: EU Member States, test sites in six countries. Format and access: EUSPA and Commission web pages, EENA webinar and CORDIS project reports, free; the service is free to national authorities. Caveats: results come from the organisers; take-up depends on phones supporting the messages. Simulation uses: emergency communication chains that bypass damaged networks, warning coverage modelling and testbed evidence for multi-channel alerting. Related records: the QZSS DC Report is the Japanese equivalent, and the US nationwide alert test covers terrestrial channels.
